96 
 
 
 
 
 
 🎵 Plus, Carlyle's hit machine | Wednesday, November 18, 2026 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 View in browser 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
 
 Axios Pro Rata 
 
 
 
 
 By Dan Primack · Nov 18, 2026 
 
 
 ✨ Situational awareness: Anthropic is expected to price its IPO tonight and begin trading tomorrow on the Nasdaq. Don't be surprised if it defies the broader AI pullback.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Share today’s Axios Pro Rata 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 Top of the Morning 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Sam Popp for Axios

 
 
 
   
 
 We picked a kind of hectic day for Axios BFD . Nvidia's first post-Jensen earnings. The eve of Anthropic pricing its IPO. Everything breaking.

 A huge thanks to the hundreds of readers who joined us in person, the thousands who joined virtually, our speakers, and our entire Axios Live crew. As always, please send any feedback my way . I'm still processing everything, but some quick hits: New York Fed president John Williams said the AI boom could push the central bank to raise interest rates next year. But he downplayed the need for a half-percentage-point rate hike next month.

 He also said the Fed is paying close attention to how the AI industry is financing itself: "You're looking for where's the leverage and where are the complex structures that maybe create unexpected disruptions in markets. But right now, we're not seeing that." Alex Rodriguez doesn't believe that Major League Baseball will play a full season in 2027, but does believe there's a deal to be had between the players and owners so long as the phrase "salary cap" isn't part of it.

 He also suggested that he'd be interested in buying another pro sports team in Minnesota, in addition to his co-ownership of the NBA's Timberwolves and WNBA's Lynx — deals he pursued after failing to buy the New York Mets. "I thank God every day for Steve Cohen for buying the Mets. I send him a Christmas card." Kim Posnett, co-head of investment banking at Goldman Sachs, doesn't think AI is a bubble but does see "mini-bubbles" where capital has gotten out far ahead of revenue. 

 She also believes the IPO market is healthier than some might believe — in part due to the diversity of 2026 issuers — but acknowledges that many issuers have stayed on the sidelines due to volatility driven by Iran war, midterms, persistent inflation, and rising rates. On the moment she knew her team had won the lead on SpaceX's IPO: "I think the moment we realized we won was at the very end." Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour said he opposes the CFTC's decision to indefinitely ban it from allowing traders to bet on the words President Trump says in public, but that Kalshi did take down "mention markets" at the CFTC's request.

 "What the president does say moves markets. So predicting what he's about to say is actually pretty meaningful." Chris Sacca of Lowercarbon Capital acknowledged that "climate" has become a dirty word, but notes that other VCs and financial institutions are very interested in the exact same companies if framed as "energy" and "advanced manufacturing."

 He also supports the permitting bill , arguing that environmentalists too often are what stands in the way of environmental progress. "We don't hire climate people. They tend to find science projects and then try and convince themselves and each other that it's gonna be a real business. And they burn out really quickly. If all you're doing is constantly thinking about the existential crises facing the planet ... you eventually just get toasted. So we work with people who love to build stuff, who love to dig into hard science, who like to solve intractable problems and, at the end, we use climate as a proxy for world positivity." I'll have takeaways from other speakers tomorrow, and also what I heard on the sidelines... 

 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 The BFD 
 
 
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios

 
 
 
   
 
 Litmus Music, a music rights platform whose portfolio includes songs by Katy Perry and Keith Urban, secured $475 million in equity funding from KKR and founding backer Carlyle Global Credit .

 Why it's the BFD: This suggests that Wall Street isn't close to running out of popular artists who are ready and willing to sell their old work.

 Elsewhere: Duetti, a separate music rights investment group, secured $665 million in financing from Carlyle, Viola Credit, Flexpoint Ford, and Truist Bank. 

 The bottom line: Remember when Taylor Swift complained about a Carlyle-backed group buying her masters, and it seemed that the firm would be persona non grata in the music biz? Neither does the music biz.

 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 Venture Capital Deals 
 
 
   
 
 🚑 Isomorphic Labs , an AI drug discovery startup led by Demis Hassabis, raised $5b in Series C funding. Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital led, joined by a16z and Alphabet. axios.link/4t57ML4 

 • Payhawk , a London-based spend management platform, raised $280m in Series C funding. Goldman Sachs led, joined by QED, Greenoaks, Lightspeed, Hedosophia, Bek Ventures, Galdana Ventures, Cogito Capital, Invus, and Inveready. axios.link/3UJwowq 

 🚑 Hone Health , a New York-based telehealth startup focused on longevity care, raised $228m in Series A extension funding. General Catalyst 's Customer Value Fund provided $200m in nondilutive funding, while MarcyPen Capital Partners led a $28m equity raise that also included Kinship Ventures, Pentland Ventures, Hanwha, Gannet Capital, Humbition, and Comma. axios.link/4AEVw6G 

 🚀 Ramon.Space , an Israeli space computing infrastructure company, raised $124m in Series B funding. PSG led, joined by Micron Technology, Senvest, Phoenix Financial, StageOne, Deep Insight, and Grove Ventures. axios.link/4iQq3ac 

 🚑 Marrow Therapeutics , a Watertown, Mass.-based biotech focused on blood disorders, raised $120m in Series B funding. OrbiMed led, joined by Scion Life Sciences, venBio, RTW Investments, Surveyor Capital, Opaleye, NEXTBio Capital, Affinity Advisors, KKR, Spruce Street Capital, and Columbia Threadneedle Investments. axios.link/3Vzn4eL 

 🚑 VitriVax , a Boulder, Colo.-based developer of a Lyme disease vaccine, raised $87m in Series C funding from F-Prime, NEA, RA Capital Management, Sanofi Ventures, and Eli Lilly. axios.link/3UUnpIQ 

 • LanceDB , an SF-based AI database developer, raised $57.5m in Series B funding. Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors led, joined by Theory Ventures, Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV, and YC. axios.link/4iRfSna 

 🚑 Knit Health , a patient referrals optimization startup, raised $35m in Series A funding. NEA led, joined by Town Hall Ventures and SignalFire. axios.link/4AG4vEJ 

 🚀 Dcubed , a German space hardware startup, raised €27.2m in Series A+ funding. Warsaw Equity Group led, joined by European Innovation Council, HTGF, BayBG, and Expansion. axios.link/4zspWYQ 

 🌎 Traitomic , a Danish developer of gene-screening tech for plants and microbes, raised €20m in Series A funding. Sofinnova Partners led, joined by Export and Investment Fund of Denmark, Footprint Firm, Nordic Foodtech VC, PSV Hafnium, and SVG Ventures. axios.link/4zNSQUc 

 • Speakeasy , a software platform for live entertainment, raised $18.8m in Series A funding, per Axios Pro . VMG Technology led, joined by Capital One Ventures, Positive Sum, and Yamaha Music Innovation Fund. axios.link/3XfJWjU 

 • Sequel.io , a San Jose, Calif.-based audience intelligence startup, raised $15m, per Axios Pro . Sorenson Capital led, joined by High Alpha, Album VC, Webflow Ventures, Javelin Venture Partners, Struck Capital, Alumni Ventures, and Social Leverage. axios.link/3UDkjZF 

 • Voyage Labs , a personal AI agent focused on travel, raised $12m in seed funding. Kleiner Perkins led, joined by SignalFire and SV Angel. axios.link/3XyS0wc 

 🌎 Zya , a U.K. producer of enzymes to convert food sugars into fiber, raised £11.5m in Series A funding. Astanor led, joined by Ahren Innovation Capital, Red Bull Ventures, Zubi Capital, Phase Change, and Meach Cove Capital. axios.link/4fdri2i 

 • Iconic , a Dutch project infrastructure management startup, raised $10m in seed funding. Peak Capital led, joined by Bridford Group, Common Magic, Graduate Ventures, NP-Hard, and Tiny VC. axios.link/4knZgEW 

 • Aarden , a Seattle-based provider of land use software, raised $8m. Overture led, joined by Madrona and Propeller. axios.link/4iYBJaW 

 • Pretxt , an enterprise AI supervision startup, raised $5m in seed funding from Deciens Capital, Howdy Partners, NSV Wolf Capital, and Service Provider Capital. axios.link/4fbEPaE 

 • Global Kiwi Labs , an exchange infrastructure startup for digital assets, raised $4m in seed funding. Valor Capital Group led, joined by Adderall Capital, Keyrock, and Staking Facilities. axios.link/4B0m02T 

 🚑 AstraNu , a Murray Hill, N.J.-based provider of optical coherence tomography imaging for medical devices, raised $3.5m in seed funding. Celesta Capital led, joined by New Jersey Innovation Evergreen Fund. axios.link/4zS475P 

 • Newsbound , an Israel-based PR platform, raised $3m in pre-seed funding. Joule Ventures and State of Mind Ventures led, joined by 91 Ventures. axios.link/4t8PAAq 

 • Perry AI , a London-based legal-tech startup, raised $2.2m in seed funding. Haatch led, joined by Antler, Syncorp Ventures, and Arāya Ventures. axios.link/4jnhfdw 

 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 Private Equity Deals 
 
 
   
 
 ⚡️ AEGIS Hedging Solutions , owned by Goldman Sachs , ageed to acquire Uplift Energy Strategy , a Denver-based energy advisory. axios.link/4t5c5Ge 

 • Centerbridge Partners acquired Amplix , a Norwood, Mass.-based tech advisory, from Gemspring Capital . axios.link/4fGtZJV 

 • Clearwave , backed by GTCR and Berkshire Partners , agreed to acquire the Ting Internet fiber assets of Tucows (Nasdaq: TCS). axios.link/4eH1efM 

 ⚡️ EQT agreed to acquire Flatiron Energy , a Denver-based energy storage company, from Hull Street Energy . axios.link/4CgVlQL 

 🚑 Frazier Healthcare Partners acquired a majority stake in ATUM , a Newark, Calif.-based provider of contract research services for biotech. axios.link/48ZUJBn 

 🚑 KKR completed its $5.7b take-private buyout of Integer (NYSE: ITGR), a Plano, Texas-based medical device outsourcer. axios.link/3S5OVS9 

 • Partners Group acquired a majority stake in French beauty and wellness retailer Aroma-Zone from Eurazeo (which retains a position). axios.link/4C8MKiJ 

 ⚡️ Regency Electric , an MFG Partners portfolio company, acquired Tekline Electrical Services , a Chandler, Ariz.-based commercial and industrial electrical contractor. axios.link/4zrJpc0 

 • Sixth Street invested $350m for a minority stake in meat snack brand Chomps . Existing backers include Stride Consumer Partners. axios.link/4CbbKpH 

 • Southfield Capital formed Cavalry , a commercial towing and recovery platform in the Midwestern U.S. axios.link/4zS8KwJ 

 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 Liquidity Events 
 
 
   
 
 🚑 Astromech is acquiring fellow Colossal Biosciences spinoff Form Bio for $230m in stock, per Axios Pro . Astromech, valued at $3.8b in August, plans to raise funding next year. Form Bio had raised $64m from firms like Caladan Capital, Saraswati Ventures, Calm Ventures, and Jazz Venture Partners. axios.link/4khCn5U 

 🚑 EQT is weighing a sale of Indian fertility services firm Indira IVF Hospitals , per Bloomberg. axios.link/3WLEzZO 

 🚑 UPS (NYSE: UPS) agreed to acquire Smartways Logistics, a provider of health-care logistics in Australia and New Zealand, from The Riverside Co. axios.link/4iYJUnT 

 • Workday (Nasdaq: WDAY) agreed to acquire Honeydew , a semantic layer for AI and business intelligence that had raised $26m from firms like Footwork and Daybreak. axios.link/3WJ4Vvq 

 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 More M&A 
 
 
   
 
 • Carlisle Cos. (NYSE: CSL) agreed to acquire PermaTherm , a Monticello, Ga.-based manufacturer of insulated metal panels and accessories. axios.link/4Azmqg7 

 ⚡️ EnQuest (LSE: ENQ) agreed to sell its U.K. upstream business to NEO Next+ , a unit of TotalEnergies (Paris: TTE), for $960m. axios.link/4iYF0ae 

 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 Fundraising 
 
 
   
 
 🚑 Blue Sea Capital , a health-care PE firm based in Florida, raised $800m for its fourth fund. axios.link/4kZ8wiQ 

 • Stage 2 Capital , a VC firm focused on early-stage B2B AI startups, raised a total of $100m for a pair of new funds. stage2.capital 

 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 It's Personnel 
 
 
   
 
 ⚡️ Noel Black joined Energy Impact Partners as chief utility officer. He previously was with Algonquin Power & Utilities. axios.link/3UJvrUS 

 • Zoe Clements joined BGF as a non-executive director. She previously held top PE roles at Palatine Private Equity, Electra Partners, and LGV Capital. axios.link/4Cf2T6w 

 ⚡️ Aaron Klein joined Vision Ridge Partners as head of capital markets. He previously was with Lincoln International. axios.link/4j5CEGT 

 • Emma Mann-Meginniss joined Davis Polk as a partner in the capital markets practice. She previously was with Cooley. axios.link/4AxZP3A 

 • Mandeep Singh , Trouva co-founder, joined London-based Tapestry VC as a general partner. axios.link/4AIlE0E 

 
 
   
 
   
 
 
 🎳 Final Numbers 
 
 
   
 
 Data: Financial Modeling Prep ; Chart: Dan Primack/Axios Lucky Strike Entertainment stock jumped 22% yesterday after founder and CEO Thomas Shannon proposed taking the company private for $4.35 per share.

 Lucky Strike owns bowling centers, the Professional Bowlers Association, and water parks. It went public in 2021 via SPAC merger. The company doesn't appear to be benefiting from the broader rise in experiential entertainment, likely due to inflationary pressures.
